title: Rabbah bar Kirya

paragraphs: Mentioned in Kilayim, chapter 9, at the end of halakhah 4 [compare 9:3], walking with Rabbi Elazar in Aistron, etc. Hyman proposes this reading there, as the statement appears in Ketubot, chapter 12, at the end of halakhah 3.

notes.text: The cited walking passage was not found in the bounded consulted Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:4 text. The historical locator and Aistron wording are retained without imposing a new location.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Kilayim chapter9 scalar in halakhah index2 (9:3) has Rabbi Barkirya and Elazar walking in Aistrin. The whole Ketubot12:3 parallel separates Rabbi bar Kirya. These match the walking account alongside Hyman’s end-of-halakhah4 citation, but source Rabbah bar Kirya and Aistron are not silently normalized to that edition’s names or geography. The proposed adoption of the parallel remains Hyman’s judgment.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1083) gives the end of Kilayim 9:4 and the end of Ketubot 12:3. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3 writes the name as Rabbi Barkirya, and Ketubot 12:3 separates it as Rabbi bar Kirya. Both give Aistrin for the place where he and Rabbi Elazar were walking. The heading Rabbah bar Kirya and the form Aistron follow Hyman.
